previous_disclosures.summary: The company identifies four reportable business units: Compute and Networking (CNBU), Mobile (MBU), Embedded (EBU), and Storage (SBU), each comprising specific memory, storage, and networking products for defined markets.

current_disclosures.summary: Segment information is consistent with how it is reviewed and evaluated by the chief operating decision maker, with four reportable business units identified.
The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
The Mobile Business Unit includes memory and storage products sold into the smartphone and other mobile-device markets.
The Embedded Business Unit includes memory and storage products and solutions sold into the intelligent edge through the automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets.
The Storage Business Unit includes SSDs and component-level storage solutions sold into the data center, PC, and consumer markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the composition of their reportable segments focused on computing and data center hardware. MU defines its Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) as including memory products and solutions for data centers, PCs, and networking. AMD defines its Data Center segment as primarily including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, APUs, DPUs, and FPGAs for data centers. While MU focuses on memory solutions within this segment and AMD focuses on processors and accelerators, both explicitly include data center applications in their primary computing segments.

comparisons.peer_summary: The semiconductor solutions segment provides devices for data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking, as well as products for mobile, set-top box, broadband access, storage, industrial, and automotive markets. The segment also includes IP licensing.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe semiconductor solutions targeting data center and networking applications. MU's CNBU includes memory products for data center and networking markets. Broadcom's semiconductor solutions segment explicitly provides devices for data center and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking. Both identify data center and networking as key market drivers for their respective semiconductor offerings, though MU specifies memory products while Broadcom specifies AI networking and connectivity devices.

comparisons.comparison: While INTC does not use the 'Compute and Networking' segment label, it discloses reportable segments that map to similar computing functions but with a different organizational structure. INTC reports Client Computing Group (CCG) and Data Center and AI (DCAI) as reportable segments. MU groups its data center memory and PC memory into a single CNBU, whereas INTC separates Client (PC/Client) and Data Center/AI. Both disclosures address the same underlying business drivers (data center and client computing) but structure the reporting differently, with MU combining them and INTC splitting them.
